```{r}
#| label: Load data and specify fixed effects formula
setwd("../data_tidy/")

frame <- readRDS("gradients_lb.RDS")
fixed_effects <- "group + age + sex"
```

Projection of 7 functional networks defined by Yeo et al. on ROIs defined by Glasser et al.

```{r}
#| label: Plot yeo networks
dt_yeo <- frame %>%
  dplyr::distinct(region, yeo, hemi)

cmap_yeo <- c(
  visual = "#781286", 
  sensorimotor = "#4682B4", 
  'dorsal attention' = "#00760E", 
  'ventral attention' = "#C43AFA",
  limbic = "#DCF8A4", 
  frontoparietal = "#E69422", 
  'default mode' = "#CD3E4E"
)

dt_yeo$yeo <- plyr::revalue(dt_yeo$yeo, c(
  "VN" = "visual", 
  "SMN" = "sensorimotor", 
  "DAN" = "dorsal attention",
  "VAN" = "ventral attention",
  "LN" = "limbic",
  "FPN" = "frontoparietal",
  "DMN" = "default mode"
))

dt_yeo$yeo <- factor(dt_yeo$yeo, levels = names(cmap_yeo))

yeo_plot <- ggplot(data = dt_yeo) +
  geom_brain(
    atlas = glasser(),
    # position = position_brain(view + hemi ~ .),
    position = position_brain(c(
      "right lateral",
      "right medial",
      "left lateral",
      "left medial"
    )),
    aes(fill = yeo),
    size = 0.05
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  # scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cmap_yeo, name = "") +
  theme(legend.key.size = unit(0.25, 'cm'))
print(yeo_plot)
```

# Connectivity gradients across neocortex

## ROI analyses

```{r paged.print = FALSE}

stats_lm <- frame %>%
  group_by(region, hemi, yeo, gradient, stream) %>%
  do({
    model <- lm(as.formula(paste("gradient_score ~", fixed_effects)), data = .)
    
    # Extract group coefficient only
    tidy(model) %>%
      filter(grepl("^group", term))  # Keep only group effect
  }) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  rename(
    coefficient = estimate,
    statistic = statistic
  )

# Apply FDR correction per gradient
stats_corrected <- stats_lm %>%
  group_by(gradient) %>%
  mutate(p_adjust = p.adjust(p.value, method = "fdr")) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(p_adjust < 0.05)

# extract min and max for plotting
min_val <- min(stats_corrected$statistic)
max_val <- max(stats_corrected$statistic)

stats_g1 <- stats_corrected %>%
  dplyr::filter(gradient == "gradient_1") %>%
  arrange(yeo, stream) %>%
  mutate_if(is.numeric, round, digits = 3) %>%
  mutate(across(c(p.value, p_adjust), ~ ifelse(. < 0.001, "< 0.001", as.character(.)))) %>%
  select(-gradient, -term) %>%
  rename("p (uncorr)" = p.value, "p (corr)" = p_adjust) 

# write.csv(stats_g1, "../results/table_s01.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}

                     by = .(group, yeo, region, gradient, hemi, stream)]

gradient1_df <- sum_group %>%
  filter(gradient == "gradient_1") %>%
  group_by(group)

g1_plot3 <- plot_2_groups(gradient1_df)
g1_plot3
```

## Community-based profiles

To summarise the findings from the ROI analysis, we applied a well-established functional community decomposition (see Methods)49. Then we conducted a network-based z-score analysis of gradient scores for each of the first three gradients. In G1 and G2, the late blind group did not significantly differ from the sighted control group (all group x network interactions p > .05). In G3, we observed that the group of late blind individuals had lower gradient scores in the visual network than sighted controls. This is similar to what we observed for congenitally blind individuals.

### Gradient 1

Distribution of the gradient scores for each of the 7 functional networks (transparent distribution: group of blind individuals, non-transparent distribution: group of sighted controls). The tick below the density plots represents the mean gradient score.

```{r}
sum_community <- frame[, .(mean_grad = mean(gradient_score)),
                         by = .(subject, group, yeo, gradient, age, sex)]

gradient_1 <- sum_community[gradient == "gradient_1", ]

grad1_plot <- create_dist_plot(gradient_1)
grad1_plot
```

Results of the network-based z-score analysis of gradient scores.

```{r paged.print = FALSE, warning=FALSE}
community_g1 <- sum_community[gradient == "gradient_1", ]

model1 <- mixed(as.formula(paste("mean_grad ~ yeo * ", fixed_effects, "+ (1|subject)")), data = community_g1)
model1

```

Estimated marginal means for each groupxnetwork combination.

```{r paged.print=FALSE}
emm_int <- emmeans(model1, ~ group | yeo)

emm_int_df <- summary(emm_int) %>%
  data.table() %>%
  dplyr::mutate_if(is.numeric, round, 3)
emm_int_df

```

Post-hoc tests assessing the effect of group on mean gradient scores of each Yeo network.

```{r paged.print=FALSE}
post_emm_int <- update(pairs(emm_int), adjust = "holm")
post_df <- data.table(summary(post_emm_int))
post_emm_int <- summary(post_emm_int) %>%
  data.table()  %>%
  dplyr::mutate_if(is.numeric, round, 3)
post_emm_int
```

Group differences in the mean gradient scores across 7 functional networks. Significant differences are shown with full color, whereas non-significant differences are shown with transparent color.

```{r}
grad3_lolli_plot <- create_lolli_plot(post_emm_int, t.ratio, yeo, cmap_yeo)
grad3_lolli_plot
```

## Between-network distances

In the next step, we tested for potential group differences in the distance of the visual network and the rest of the networks. In G1 and G2, we did not observe group differences in the distance between the visual network and the rest of the networks. In G3, the visual network of late blind individuals was closer to the ventral attention, dorsal attention, and frontoparietal networks than the visual network of sighted controls, similar to what we observed for congenitally blind individuals.

### Gradient 1

LMM Results: No significant group x network interaction.

```{r}
# Calculate the mean gradient for yeo == "VN" for each subject and group
vn_means <- gradient_1 %>%
  filter(yeo == "VN") %>%
  group_by(subject, group) %>%
  summarise(vn_mean_grad = mean(mean_grad, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop')

# Join the means with the original dataframe
vn_distance <- gradient_1 %>%
  group_by(subject, group, yeo, age, sex) %>%
  summarise(mean_grad = mean(mean_grad, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  left_join(vn_means, by = c("subject", "group")) %>%
  mutate(diff_vn = abs(mean_grad - vn_mean_grad)) %>%
  filter(yeo != "VN") %>%
  ungroup()

model1 <- mixed(as.formula(paste("diff_vn ~ yeo * ", fixed_effects, "+ (1|subject)")), data = vn_distance)
model1
```

### Gradient 2

LMM Results: significant group x network interaction.

```{r}
# Calculate the mean gradient for yeo == "VN" for each subject and group
vn_means <- gradient_2 %>%
  filter(yeo == "VN") %>%
  group_by(subject, group) %>%
  summarise(vn_mean_grad = mean(mean_grad, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop')

# Join the means with the original dataframe
vn_distance <- gradient_2 %>%
  group_by(subject, group, yeo, age, sex) %>%
  summarise(mean_grad = mean(mean_grad, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  left_join(vn_means, by = c("subject", "group")) %>%
  mutate(diff_vn = abs(mean_grad - vn_mean_grad)) %>%
  filter(yeo != "VN") %>%
  ungroup()

model1 <- mixed(as.formula(paste(
  "diff_vn ~ yeo * ", fixed_effects, "+ (1|subject)"
)), data = vn_distance)
model1
```

Estimated marginal means

```{r paged.print=FALSE}
emm_int <- emmeans(model1, ~ group | yeo)

emm_int_df <- summary(emm_int) %>%
  data.table() %>%
  dplyr::mutate_if(is.numeric, round, 3)
emm_int_df
```

Post-hoc tests: We did not observe significant differences between the groups in the distance of the visual network and the rest of the networks.

```{r paged.print=FALSE}
post_emm_int <- update(pairs(emm_int), adjust = "holm")
post_df <- data.table(summary(post_emm_int))
post_emm_int <- summary(post_emm_int) %>%
  data.table()  %>%
  dplyr::mutate_if(is.numeric, round, 3)
post_emm_int
```
